subject: Observability crediting structure and dashboard bundling inquiry
messages:
From: Simone Park <simone@atlasplatform.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Murphy <liam.murphy@atlasplatform.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-on: retention/tracing/dashboard pricing question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Atlas liked the dashboard previews and the tracing demo. Before we move to a POC, procurement asked for clarity on how observability add-ons are priced for retention and traces. Specific asks:

- Can retention be credited back when we roll over long-term storage?
- How do you tier tracing credits vs. active traces?
- Is there a bundled price for the advanced dashboards + traces vs buy‑separate?

We have an internal goal to cap add-on spend to ~20% of our model inference bill in year one. If you have a short example invoice or a simple pricing ladder, that would help.

Also, can you outline any concession paths for startups that hit commit thresholds?

Thanks,
Simone
Simone Park
Director of Platform Engineering, Atlas Platform
simone@atlasplatform.com

-----
Note: attaching a small sample of our metric ingestion (attached as atlas_usage_sample.csv)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Simone Park <simone@atlasplatform.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on: retention/tracing/dashboard pricing question

Hi Simone — great to hear Atlas liked the demo. Quick answers up front, and I attached a short pricing cheat sheet: RW_addons_pricing_v1.pdf.

- Retention credits: we offer rollover credits for archival up to 12 months if you purchase an annual retention bundle; beyond that archival is billed at a reduced egress rate. Rollover policy depends on the committed term.
- Tracing credits: we meter active trace ingestions (spans/day) and provide tiered credits that scale with committed throughput. Credits are consumed before pay‑as‑you‑go.
- Bundling: yes — advanced dashboards + tracing can be bundled at a blended per-seat + usage rate that typically saves ~15–25% vs separate line items depending on commit.

Concessions: we commonly offer a short promotional discount on the first quarter of add-on fees (one quarter free or 25% off) in exchange for a 12‑month minimum on the addon commit. For larger deals we can structure a mix of up-front credits and quarterly rebates tied to usage.

Ben (copied) has run similar deals — Ben, any sample invoice or a concise breakdown you can share?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.ai

Attachment: RW_addons_pricing_v1.pdf (stub)

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on: retention/tracing/dashboard pricing question

Hi Simone — I put together a short sample invoice and two concession scenarios based on Atlas numbers in the CSV you sent. High level:

Scenario A (Conservative commit)
- 12 month retention bundle (200 TB ingest-equivalent): $18k/mo
- Tracing tier (mid): $6k/mo with 200k spans/day credits included
- Advanced dashboards (seat-based): $2k/mo for 5 seats
- Total addons (pre-discount): $26k/mo
- Concession: 1 month free retention + 25% off dashboards in Q1 if you sign 12 months -> effective Q1: $20.5k/mo

Scenario B (Higher commit, negotiated)
- 24 month uplift with 10% committed discount across retention + traces
- Additional 3 months of tracing credits up-front if you commit by end of quarter
- Can include an SLA-linked credit clause: 0.5% credit of monthly addon invoice if retention availability drops below 99.9% for the month

I attached the detailed sample invoice and a redlineable SOW (proposed_sow_atlas_v2.pdf). For procurement: typical billing is monthly with net30; we can evaluate net45 for enterprise procurement if needed.

Let me know which scenario you want to pilot; we can shorten the promo window for Q4 closes.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed_sow_atlas_v2.pdf (stub), sample_invoice_atlas.csv (stub)

Thanks Ben — helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

1) Need the SLA-linked credit language in the SOW to be explicit (monthly credit calculation and how credits are applied to invoices).
2) Atlas is comfortable with a 12-month commit, but the add-on baseline needs to be capped as a percentage of the overall monthly invoice (we proposed 20%). If addons exceed 20% in any quarter, we want a 10% cap on incremental growth or an automatic review.
3) Can you provide an example of what “tracing credits” look like operationally (how we monitor consumption, how credits are deducted)?

Procurement prefers net45, and they want to see a one-page summary we can attach to the PO. Can you send that?

-Liam
Liam Murphy

liam.murphy@atlasplatform.com

Subject: Re: Observability add-on: retention/tracing/dashboard pricing question

Liam — appreciate the specifics. Quick reply with an actionable, procurement-ready package attached and the operational notes inline.

1) SOW credit language: added a short clause — "Monthly SLA credits for retention availability will be calculated as 0.5% of the monthly add-on invoice for every 0.1% below 99.9% Retention Availability, up to a maximum of 5% of the add-on invoice." This will appear in page 3 of the attached proposed_sow_atlas_v2.pdf.

2) Add-on cap: we can add a contractual clause to cap add-ons to 20% of the combined Redwood monthly invoice for the first 12 months. If add-ons exceed that threshold in any calendar quarter, Redwood will (a) pause automatic scaling of add-on ingestion until a joint review and (b) offer a 10% discount on incremental overage for the next month while we conduct the review.

3) Tracing credits: operational notes — we expose a credits dashboard in the Console (Admin -> Billing -> Addon Credits) showing current balance, daily consumption, and alert thresholds. Credits are deducted in this order: promotional credits, committed credits, pay-as-you-go. We will provide a sample telemetry webhook that posts daily consumption to your endpoint so you can reconcile.

Procurement package attached: one-page summary (onepage_atlas_addons.pdf), updated SOW (proposed_sow_atlas_v2.pdf), and the sample telemetry CSV. We also note net45 as the preferred term and will mark that on the quote; finance approval is needed but we can route.

If that works, Jasmine — can you get internal sign-off on the net45 exception and the Q1 promotional concession (1 month free retention + 25% dashboards)? If so we will circulate the final quote for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai
